newsitem.title: USA: CBOT Sep contract expirations may be expolsive.
newsitem.headline: CBOT Sep contract expirations may be expolsive.

text.p: The potential exists for an explosive expiration Thursday for the Chicago Board of Trade September grain and soy contracts, especially for September wheat and corn, traders said.
"I think it will be explosive on corn and wheat. Both of the open interest numbers are high," said Steve Bruce of E.D. and F. Man International.

The CBOT September contracts are slated to expire Thursday at 1201 CDT. Before trading Wednesday, the open interest in September wheat stood at 7.6 million bushels and September corn was at 15.97 million bushels, according to the CBOT.

"Those numbers should be down around two million for wheat and five million for corn by now. If these go out as gentle as a lamb it will be a surprise to me," said Paul Moravek, trading specialist for LFG Futures.
There's no doubt the open interest in the September for each commodity already has been drawn down with traders actively getting out of that month.
September wheat was strongly higher as of 1238 CDT after moving in a 9-1/2 cent per bushel trading range.
"They're busy getting out over there," a trader said referring to the liquidation in the September wheat.
They said the September wheat contract was higher because Continental Grain stopped all of the 700,000 bushels of wheat posted Wednesday against the September contract.

September corn also was firm on the posting of no deliveries on the September and as of late Tuesday there were only 5,000 bushels of corn registered for possible delivery, all of it in Chicago warehouses.
"With no corn in town (deliverable stocks) that's a high number (corn open interest)," Bruce said.
But some traders also said the potential for a volatile expiration also exists in the soybean complex, with the posting of no deliveries on the CBOT September soybean contract.
"Those are big open interest numbers all across the Septembers," said Mark Cermak of O'Connor and Co.
CBOT data showed as of early Wednesday the open interest in September soybeans was at 6.005 million bushels, soymeal 2,888 contracts and 927 contracts were open in soyoil.
"Those are pretty big numbers going into expiration day, it has the potential to be explosive," Cermak said.
